title: Library Happenings: Tech, the paranormal and entertainment converge at the library

content:
October 12, 2026 at 8:01 AM

Did you know that Superior Public Library offers free technology programs especially for older adults? Our popular Senior Planet program introduces older adults to a variety of tech topics through fun and interactive classes. Upcoming topics include "Intro to iPhones" on Thursday, Oct. 15, "Podcasts at a Glance" on Oct. 22, and "Staying in Touch as Landlines Change" on Nov. 12. Senior Planet classes start at 2 p.m. and no registration is required. Thanks to the Rotary Club of Superior for its support of our Senior Planet programs.

Do you have a question about your smartphone, tablet or laptop? Bring it to one of the library's free Device Advice sessions and get one-on-one assistance with common device questions like texting, using apps, adjusting settings and more. Device Advice will be held Thursday, Oct. 15 and Oct. 29 from 10:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. and Oct. 28 from 4:30 to 6:30 p.m. No registration required. Assistance will be provided on a first-come, first-served basis.

Come to the library on Oct. 19 at 5:30 p.m. for a free program with musician Yuya Mix and enjoy a variety of popular Japanese music from the world of anime, covers of English tunes, and contemporary songs. Learn about the cultural significance of these songs as well as the lyrics and meanings of each selection. Thanks to the Superior Public Library Foundation for supporting this program.

Duluth Paranormal Society returns to Superior Public Library on Oct. 20 at 5:30 p.m. when they'll share evidence from previous investigations, demonstrate the equipment they use during ghost hunts, and talk about their experiences. Refreshments will be provided by the Friends of the Library.

The Douglas County Drug Prevention Coalition will hold its free annual fall Drug Take-Back Day on Oct. 23 from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. at the library. This event offers a confidential, safe and responsible way to dispose of unused or expired medications. Members of the Douglas County Drug Prevention Coalition will be onsite providing free resources, medication lock boxes and Deterra medication disposal bags. Stop by, drop off your old medications, and help keep our community safe and healthy.

The library will show free movies in October and November. On Oct. 26, join us for “Disclosure Day” (PG-13). On Nov. 9, we’ll show “The Mandalorian and Grogu” (PG-13) and on Nov. 23, join us for “Breadwinner” (PG). All movies start at 6 p.m. and closed captions will be enabled.

Sue Heskin is the director of the Superior Public Library.
